summary: Reuse the complete 004DCAA0 record-array clear body for existing resize-to-zero operations on the actual particle-clock record vector.

rows.reason: Each existing resize(actual_vector, actual_resize_context, 0) becomes one call to the existing PUSH0/CALL004DC410/RET body; actual vector, context, record cleanup and free ordering are preserved.
Already entry-reachable before the change; it supplies the real vector and context to the newly wired clear body, so no additional release-all invocation is needed.
No separately emitted Release symbol; its existing inlined ArrayCleanup path supplies the new clear-body call and retains the subsequent current-data free.
No separately emitted Release symbol; its existing inlined scalar-delete path supplies the new clear-body call after disarming array cleanup.
Missing the frame-job-thread deferred-call producer and its real source LuaVariantRecord vector; the main-thread interpreter's queue_call remains unimplemented.
Missing a live MovCamZoom owner and original zoom-command adapter; the existing mission camera projection cannot supply that state.
Missing a reached helm-control message application with real sender authority, timestamp and backfill consumer; the earlier c750 review remains applicable.
Missing a host-owned actual NativeBotStateRegistryStorage and reached approach/state-machine constructor binding.
Missing the same live registry owner and its destruction binding; constructing a temporary registry would invent state.
Missing a live consumer of the original previous-timestamp field; the source search found only the existing getter and method-table inventory.

measurements.before_call_graph_note: The initial who query used an older cached graph; no current baseline aggregate called count is claimed. The post-build graph was regenerated.

validation: Baseline and post-change ./scripts/build.ps1 passed all four existing tests.
python tools/call_graph.py refreshed the Release executable graph after the successful build.
python tools/call_graph.py who 004dcaa0 reports REACHABLE, three call sites, three live callers and zero unreachable callers.
python tools/call_graph.py path 004dcaa0 reaches the body through singleton-manager destruction and GameSingletonHost::shutdown from WinMain.
python tools/wire_readiness.py --standins reports 004dcaa0 state=wired, called=true, call_sites=3.
evidence: python tools/bsp.py show 004dcaa0 --asm: original inclusive 004DCAA0..004DCAA7 is PUSH0/CALL004DC410/RET, actual vector ECX and no original stack arguments.
python tools/bsp.py show 004dda40, 004ddaa0 and 004de290: all three original cleanup sites resize the actual record vector to zero at the replaced operation.

src/game_native_renderer_application.cpp: NativeParticleClockShutdownContext borrows the real string/record services, decrement import, particle-clock publication, current native cache profiles and resource-owner domain, and is attached to host.native_deletion_bindings().particle_clock.
scope: Source composition through the existing body, not a newly established original caller: the original cleanup sites call resize directly. No new address-suffixed implementation, ledger row, storage, float arithmetic, switch or test case was added. Each replaced resize runs once through the wrapper.
limits: Build-tested and static entry/call-site verified. The game was not run. Runtime teardown coverage, native mixed-frame exception behavior and whole-process binary parity are unvalidated.
